defined_from: training source/fix evidence only; no predictions

categories.name: A structural input delimiter is mistaken for a valid grammar component
categories.include: An established input-validation contract requires a structural component, but a substring-only test accepts that delimiter in an unrelated position; inspect normalization, accepted grammar and actual rejection contract.
categories.exclude: Security validation without an evidenced trust boundary, newly forbidden formerly supported inputs, or a claim that a substring check implements a complete URL or other grammar.
categories.notes: Scrapy accepts /foo:bar merely because it contains a colon. The new hierarchical marker/data exception rejects the witnessed relative path but still is not a parsed, anchored scheme grammar. Mutating _url before raising is unchanged; permitted non-hierarchical schemes require history review. Consolidate general validation leaves before freeze.

categories.name: URL-bearing input is resolved before required contextual normalization
categories.include: A URL-bearing attribute or header is resolved without normalization required by an established context-specific contract, producing a wrong destination; inspect raw value, effective base, normalization helper and versioned resolver semantics.
categories.exclude: Byte-encoding loss, missing base-context propagation, generic URL joining assumed broken, security destination validation, or a newly chosen tolerant interpretation without an existing contract.
categories.notes: Scrapy strips HTML5 boundary spaces from raw form action before joining. Separately, scrapy-3 chooses authority-style interpretation for triple leading slashes; that tolerance remains ambiguous pending existing-policy evidence. URL normalization is not authorization or SSRF safety; same-function successive fixes need dependence reconciliation.

categories.name: A native-value serializer unnecessarily sends scalars through text conversion
categories.include: A serializer whose existing contract preserves native scalar values applies a bytes/text-only converter to non-string leaves, aborting or losing required scalar representation; inspect exporter purpose, recursive paths and converter type checks.
categories.exclude: Text writers requiring scalar stringification, new scalar support without an old contract, encoding loss for actual strings, or claims that preserving Python values makes all downstream serializers accept them.
categories.notes: Pinned to_bytes/to_unicode reject boolean, integer, float and datetime leaves. PythonItemExporter advertises native Python values for downstream serialization; after encodes only strings and retains other leaves. This is the opposite interface direction from the XML scalar-stringification label; consolidate under a principled representation parent if useful.

categories.name: An error adapter supplies a malformed exception tuple to its result consumer
categories.include: An established error-result API requires a sys.exc_info-style type/value/traceback tuple, but an adapter swaps components and prevents required error recording; inspect the consumer and actual failing callback path.
categories.exclude: Cosmetic diagnostic wording, logging-filter migrations without an established functional contract, wrong exception classification, or assuming a traceback formatting change repairs every error-handling path.
categories.notes: The errback passes value,type,traceback to unittest.addError rather than type,value,traceback. Retained real TextTestResult regression and pinned CPython result consumer establish required error recording, unlike logging-only siblings. Nested wrapper requires closure context; no callback or exception formatter was executed.

categories.name: A command correction duplicates operands or inserts an option in an invalid position
categories.include: An existing command-correction operation composes old and suggested arguments without respecting the command's established operand/option structure, yielding a duplicated operand or invalid option placement; inspect token producer, substitution helper and retained command contract.
categories.exclude: Shell injection without an evidenced trust boundary, shell-word tokenization errors classified as delimiter parsing, new command features, or claiming a string replacement handles all quoting and option grammars.
categories.notes: Appending --staged after a diff filename is rejected; inserting it after diff repairs retained examples. Git push additionally duplicates explicit upstream arguments unless removed before composition. Full command token lists are cached/mutated in older versions and reconstructed without quoting; residual grammar and successor repairs remain explicit questions.

categories.name: A correction rule matches output without the operation state that makes it applicable
categories.include: A rule admits an existing command or successful output because of an incidental diagnostic substring instead of the required command state or instruction, leading to an inapplicable correction or failing consumer; inspect rule guard, state helper and correction consumer.
categories.exclude: Merely adding a new supported command, policy changes without an existing applicability contract, security filtering, or claiming a more specific substring is a complete structured output parser.
categories.notes: A successful branch named feature/set-upstream triggers an upstream-error rule whose generator expects a git push instruction absent from the output. no_command also needs the executable to be absent, though which does not resolve all shell aliases/functions and the new access loses an empty-token guard. Keep functional and non-security eligibility conditional.

categories.name: A parser or mutator accesses a tail element absent from an admitted short input
categories.include: A supported command with fewer components than a parser assumes reaches indexing or pop of a missing tail element, raising instead of the established skip/correction result; inspect sequence production, earlier mutations and expected short-input behavior.
categories.exclude: Forbidden malformed short inputs, empty initial-sequence access already classified separately, arbitrary IndexError suppression, or assuming one guarded tail pop validates every option-argument combination.
categories.notes: Removing terminal -u leaves no operand for the second pop; a narrow IndexError catch repairs the retained correction. git_fix_stash reads token 1 for a supported plain git command and should instead decline. Preserve successor relationship: thefuck-11 after code is exactly thefuck-9 before code.

categories.name: Generated bytestring comparison includes padding and omits logical length
categories.include: Compiler-generated equality compares a fixed backing word instead of logical bytes and length, so dirty padding changes equality or trailing zero bytes disappear; inspect storage layout, emitted comparison and security-sensitive contract use.
categories.exclude: Ordinary Python string equality, timing claims, a hashing-helper refactor that already hashed logical length, or universal smart-contract safety inferred from changing the comparison.
categories.notes: Vyper short equal-capacity bytestring path loads a whole word without length comparison. Routing equality/inequality through logical-length keccak removes the retained dirty-padding/trailing-NUL witnesses subject to hash assumptions. Compiler Python produces EVM IR; no contract was compiled or executed. Both selected functions are one family, but keccak256_helper itself already hashes the logical span.

categories.name: External contract return values bypass declared-type runtime validation
categories.include: A compiler exposes lower-trust external returndata to expressions or copies without enforcing the declared integer or dynamic-data bounds; inspect return type inference, encoding tags, allocation and actual clamp-emitting consumers.
categories.exclude: Encoding-enum retirement alone, equivalent incoming-calldata validation, unrelated compiler panics, every generated-memory defect, or assuming one return validator proves all offsets, allocations and expressions safe.
categories.notes: Vyper 049dbdc performs strict make_setter decoding at call time and removes JSON_ABI's dynamic-size validation exemption. Full fix names both complex-expression scalar validation and JSON dynamic-data bounds; keep one conservative family pending explicit issue adjudication. Helpers merely retiring enum names are not independently defective. Returndata minimum-size checking remains conditional on skip_contract_check.

categories.name: A worker closes a socket while the event-loop thread is selecting it
categories.include: A response-writing worker can synchronously close a socket retained in the event loop's select set, causing an unhandled invalid-descriptor failure across an availability boundary; inspect worker entry points, close sink, descriptor collection and error handling.
categories.exclude: Generic races without lifecycle evidence, request framing defects, new flag forwarding alone, or assuming a close-control default of True independently prevents worker closure.
categories.notes: Waitress passes do_close=False from both task-thread flush entry points through the coordinated helpers to dispatcher.send. Main-loop handle_write retains closure ownership. Existing send calls still default to closing; the mitigation is conditional on repaired worker callers. poll catches EINTR only; no race, socket or request was executed.

categories.name: Partial-read recovery re-appends data already consumed from a retained buffer
categories.include: An established partial-read recovery path appends a whole retained buffer although part was already returned, duplicating logical output; inspect unread-count bookkeeping and the recoverable-error contract.
categories.exclude: Counting duplicate entities, all decompression errors assumed recoverable, or claiming an unread-suffix slice handles a zero unread count without checking negative-zero slicing.
categories.notes: Scrapy appends GzipFile.extrabuf after read errors; older CPython retains consumed prefix and separately records extrasize. Taking the unread suffix addresses positive-unread-count replay. The -0 slice still means the full buffer; Python runtime/private-buffer compatibility and residual cases remain questions. Binary regression fixtures were not decompressed.

categories.name: A text value crosses an interface requiring bytes, or vice versa
categories.include: An existing operation supplies str to a bytes-only sink, combines text and bytes, or supplies bytes to a text-only parser under a supported runtime, raising instead of fulfilling its established contract; inspect both interface ends and runtime support.
categories.exclude: Lossy character decoding or wrong codec already classified as text encoding, new-runtime feature additions without an old support contract, or attributing protocol security merely to converting a value to bytes.
categories.notes: Scrapy Python 3 proxy Basic encoding feeds text to base64, then its header writer combines text with bytes. Sitemap robots parsing likewise feeds response.body to startswith('Sitemap:'). Tunneling transport requires byte requests. Preserve runtime/API-history eligibility questions; these are not network-security negatives. Consolidate representation/encoding leaves before freeze.

categories.name: An admitted scalar is sent unnormalized to a string serializer
categories.include: A recursive serializer accepts scalar item values but forwards non-string scalars to a text-only writer without the established textual conversion, aborting supported serialization; inspect scalar production and the actual writer.
categories.exclude: New scalar support without an existing contract, metadata-only normalization, HTML/XML security claims without a boundary, or asserting that str preserves raw byte strings and every custom object's semantics.
categories.notes: Scrapy's retained XML regression requires float, boolean, integer and datetime text. Before passes them to _xg_characters, whose Python 2 branch calls decode and whose Python 3 branch forwards directly to XMLGenerator. Unicode strings remain separate; bytes-to-str and custom serialization remain outside the witnessed negative.

categories.name: Globally configured credentials are attached outside their intended destination scope
categories.include: Request middleware automatically attaches configured credentials to destinations beyond their intended domain policy; inspect credential configuration, destination matching and generated request paths.
categories.exclude: Redirect-header retention alone, explicitly authorized all-destination credentials, or assuming a domain/subdomain policy enforces an exact scheme-host-port origin.
categories.notes: Scrapy formerly adds Basic Authorization to every request without a header. Explicit domain or first-request default constrains automatic addition; None still permits all destinations and existing headers remain unchanged. Pinned helper compares lowercased netloc with domain/suffix; ports, userinfo and first-request trust require review. Consolidate credential-boundary leaves before freeze.

categories.name: Recursive callback tracing reacquires a non-reentrant lock held by the same thread
categories.include: A callback or model tracing path can recursively re-enter an object while its non-reentrant lock remains held, blocking on same-thread reacquisition; inspect lock construction/restoration, acquisition scope and lower-trust model reachability.
categories.exclude: Every ordinary Lock allocation, different-thread lock-order deadlocks, arbitrary untrusted Python execution already granting equivalent capabilities, or claiming RLock bounds recursion and all model resource consumption.
categories.notes: TensorFlow changes both Function layers and state restoration to RLock. _call/_initialize and graph creation retain locks while tracing callbacks. Constructors need consumer context; all three selected functions share one CVE/fix, and a retained regression expects RecursionError rather than unlimited successful recursion.

categories.name: Presence of an unrelated allowed token bypasses required whole-message filtering
categories.include: A whole-message security/moderation filter returns an allowed result merely because an unrelated permitted token is present, skipping independently prohibited content; inspect filter configuration, message provenance and enforcement consumer.
categories.exclude: Intended per-token exemptions applied only to that token, regex complexity, or assuming all messages/channels use an enabled filter or every matching message is deleted.
categories.notes: Python Discord bot exits on any URL before checking prohibited token patterns. Removing the early exit allows the remaining token to trigger configured moderation; clean_input normalizes characters but does not remove the URL. Deployment/filter policy remains contextual.

categories.name: An image data-URI exemption admits script-capable embedded content
categories.include: An HTML sanitizer exempts image data URIs without distinguishing script-capable SVG/XML content, allowing active content through the sanitization boundary; inspect MIME recognition, attribute cleaner and consuming browser/context.
categories.exclude: Ordinary HTML entity escaping, every data URI or passive image, claims of script execution in every image embedding context, or complete sanitizer safety inferred from one MIME restriction.
categories.notes: lxml Cleaner exempts data:image/...;base64 before malicious-scheme checks. New subtype XML/SVG rejection removes the retained SVG and compressed SVG data links. Pattern definitions and actual sanitizer/browser use remain required context; no payload, regex or browser was executed.

categories.name: A subprocess data argument is interpreted as an executable option
categories.include: Lower-trust data passed as an argv element can be interpreted by the invoked program as an option/configuration directive rather than the intended operand, enabling unintended capabilities; inspect option grammar, argument order and input reachability.
categories.exclude: Shell-text quoting defects, generic subprocess calls, intentionally trusted command options, or assuming argv separation prevents option injection.
categories.notes: Cookiecutter hg checkout passes checkout directly after the subcommand. Added -- terminates Mercurial option parsing for this operand; git and clone URL handling are unchanged. Retained mock assertions verify intended argv shape, not exploit reproduction or all Mercurial versions.

categories.name: Indexing dispatch bypasses required indexer dimensionality validation
categories.include: An indexing branch accepts an indexer with unsupported dimensionality through a raw extraction fallback instead of the established rejection path; inspect actual dispatch, fallback and exception/output contract.
categories.exclude: Supported new-axis operations, mere error wording, ordinary tensor reshaping defects, or assuming all multidimensional indexing is invalid.
categories.notes: Selected integer-key branch calls _get_values, whose ValueError fallback returns a raw multidimensional array; iloc enforces the retained three-dimensional-key rejection regression. This does not remove other intentionally supported raw extraction paths. Consolidate validation leaves before freeze.

categories.name: Authentication-token acceptance omits the required flow-specific algorithm policy
categories.include: An authentication-token consumer accepts an unsigned or otherwise prohibited algorithm because a required algorithm/flow policy check is absent or not invoked; inspect parser verification, trusted request context and token-return path.
categories.exclude: An unsigned token explicitly permitted on an authenticated code-flow channel, forwarding newly introduced exception context alone, or a claim that claims checks establish signature verification.
categories.notes: pyoidc rejects alg=none outside response_type=['code'] and adds client verification to Consumer.parse_authz. Algorithm defaults, upstream JWS parsing and saved authorization-request state remain contextual; same-CVE helpers are one family, not independent issues.

categories.name: Private RSA decryption exposes secret-dependent padding validity
categories.include: PKCS#1 v1.5 private decryption returns distinguishable failures or follows secret-dependent padding checks, exposing decrypted-padding validity to an observable consumer; inspect private operation, padding scan and protocol/API error propagation.
categories.exclude: Public ciphertext length/modulus rejection alone, public encryption/signature verification refactors, or assuming masked Python source is a constant-time implementation.
categories.notes: tlslite-ng replaces early padding-dependent returns with full scanning and deterministic implicit rejection. The retained patch and advisory explicitly disclaim CPython side-channel resistance: no approved constant-time or universally repaired negative follows.

categories.name: Result construction bypasses the established subclass constructor contract
categories.include: A transformation constructs a base-class result instead of the established subclass-provided result constructor, losing a required result class/API; inspect constructor hooks and a concrete result-type contract.
categories.exclude: Scalar/array dtype loss without a subclass contract, new unsupported subclass features, arbitrary metadata preservation, or assuming invoking a constructor hook propagates all metadata.
categories.notes: The final reduction branch hardcodes Series whereas another branch already uses _constructor_sliced; retained numeric/boolean reduction regressions require SubclassedSeries. Scope is this construction branch, not every reduction or metadata hook.

categories.name: A reduction requiring an element is applied to admitted empty data
categories.include: A supported empty input reaches a reduction without an identity or empty-result policy, aborting an operation that has an established empty-input result; inspect the reduction and caller/regression contract.
categories.exclude: Direct sequence indexing, forbidden empty inputs, or claims that an empty guard repairs overflow or nonempty sentinel ordering.
categories.notes: Nullable integer sorting computes min even when no missing entries need replacement; retained empty value_counts regression establishes a result. Consolidate empty-input leaves before freeze. No arbitrary NumPy/dataset code executed.

categories.name: Successive axis removal updates positions using the wrong removed coordinate
categories.include: An iterative structural transformation removes a level/axis but remaps remaining positions against the iteration counter instead of the actual removed coordinate, selecting wrong subsequent levels; inspect ordered transformations and value/axis regressions.
categories.exclude: Style-only empty-list checks, arbitrary axis ordering preferences, or incompatible measurement units without a removal/remapping mechanism.
categories.notes: MultiIndex-column unstack adjusts clocs against i rather than val. Sequential single-level unstack supplies the retained result oracle. Consolidate coordinate/context leaves using training evidence before freeze.

categories.name: A predictable shared-directory file target accepts an attacker-controlled link
categories.include: A process writes a predictable file in a shared lower-trust directory through a link-following sink, allowing a local attacker to redirect writes under the process identity; inspect path producer, actual writer, directory trust and permission preconditions.
categories.exclude: Secure atomic temporary creation, arbitrary trusted explicit file selection, or claiming moving a default into CWD guarantees safe operation in hostile directories or on existing links.
categories.notes: Keycloak CLI default /tmp/program.log reaches RotatingFileHandler. Changed relative filename also reaches os.makedirs('') in the unchanged configure_logging helper, so functioning after-code is not certified; reconcile paired-negative eligibility.

categories.name: HTTP parsing disagrees with a front end on message boundaries
categories.include: A lower-trust HTTP stream is framed differently by a backend and a relevant front end because of line delimiters, transfer-coding interpretation or invalid header normalization, permitting request-boundary desynchronization; inspect parser stages, consumed-byte handling and concrete deployment conditions.
categories.exclude: Every HTTP syntax relaxation, chunk-only hardening without demonstrated differential framing, response-header courtesy changes, or automatic cache-poisoning/authorization claims without a consuming deployment.
categories.notes: Waitress LF framing, Transfer-Encoding list fallthrough and later special-whitespace validation are related mechanisms, not independently approved issues. 16785/16786 share a mechanical family; 16789 starts from the earlier fixed parse_header hash and needs incomplete-fix lineage review.

categories.name: Lower-trust specification data is emitted as executable generated source
categories.include: A code generator inserts lower-trust specification text into source identifiers or literals without context-appropriate validation/escaping, allowing generated source syntax to be altered when subsequently imported or executed; inspect data producer, concrete template and file writer.
categories.exclude: Immediate eval already classified separately, constant import compatibility changes, or claiming generation alone executes the injected code or a quote-only fix repairs every source context.
categories.notes: Enum values supply raw uppercase keys and double-quoted literal values to enum.pyi. Supplemental exact-commit template is retained separately. New key sanitization and quote escaping leave backslash/newline context, post-sanitization collisions and default/value matching to reconcile.

categories.name: Lookup dispatch bypasses required missing-label rejection
categories.include: A label lookup is dispatched as permissive reindexing or nested selection, bypassing established rejection of absent labels; inspect key normalization, downstream validation and the existing lookup contract.
categories.exclude: Intentionally permissive reindex APIs, exception wording alone, or a new rejection policy without evidence that the old lookup contract required it.
categories.notes: Flat MultiIndex keys are wrapped into nested tuples and bypass ordinary iterable missing-label validation. Pandas-21 similarly sends non-list containers to reindex while lists use loc. API-transition history still requires explicit eligibility review.

categories.name: Transformation retains semantic metadata no longer valid for its result
categories.include: A value-changing transformation unconditionally copies semantic metadata whose invariant no longer holds, requiring invalidation or result-aware recomputation; inspect the invariant and an observable metadata contract.
categories.exclude: Required metadata lost during reconstruction, mere display changes, or assuming every transformation must discard metadata regardless of invariant preservation.
categories.notes: Calendar offset shifts can destroy original datetime spacing; timezone localization across DST likewise invalidates frequency. Retained regressions explicitly check freq; downstream functional eligibility and consolidation with metadata/context categories remain pending.

categories.name: Credential-bearing resource metadata is propagated into diagnostics
categories.include: A credential-bearing resource URI or configuration value enters an exception/log diagnostic outside its intended audience without required omission/redaction; inspect credential producer, formatting, propagation and access conditions.
categories.exclude: Nonsecret identifiers, token-bearing backend request paths classified separately, validation-only logging already covered separately, or assuming every error reaches an unauthorized reader.
categories.notes: Glance Swift single-tenant location.get_uri includes configured user/key in Duplicate/NotFound messages; multi-tenant ACL paths need separate credential-provenance proof. Keystone secret option marking is a contextual producer for DEBUG masking. Consolidate diagnostic/redaction leaves before freeze.

categories.name: Representation compatibility is mistaken for semantic type compatibility
categories.include: An operation accepts an unsupported semantic input type because it can be converted or reinterpreted at the representation level, producing values contrary to an existing reject-or-preserve contract; inspect type validation and concrete consuming conversion.
categories.exclude: Newly supported coercions, mere exception wording, supported conversions losing their required dtype already covered separately, or security input validation without a demonstrated boundary.
categories.notes: Datetime/timedelta insertion validator lets unsupported numeric/different-semantic objects reach .view(int64), reinterpreting NumPy scalar bits. Stricter validation plus matched scalar unboxing rejects incompatible labels; old string-to-object fallback is preserved separately.

categories.name: Conditional update selects positions using the wrong operand's predicate
categories.include: A selective update derives its position mask from replacement data instead of the target state whose elements may be changed, overwriting values required to remain unchanged; inspect both masks, code sentinels and the update contract.
categories.exclude: Label/position reordering alone, intended full replacement, new update features, or claiming the mask fix also guarantees copy/alias safety.
categories.notes: Categorical fillna with Series chooses nonmissing replacement codes instead of missing target codes, overwriting valid originals. New target mask preserves nonmissing values; both versions may alias self._codes and require separate mutation review.

categories.name: Dispatch omits an explicit execution option required by the consumer
categories.include: A wrapper accepts an established execution option but omits it on an existing dispatch branch, causing a functional result/order difference under the downstream default; inspect option producer, consumer and actual expected output.
categories.exclude: Warning-only forwarding, environment resource precedence, deliberately changing omitted/default values, or new optional features without an old functional contract.
categories.notes: Unique-index list joins omit sort in concat while DataFrame join forwards it. Retained regression checks unsorted index order as well as warnings; duplicate-index fallback still omits sort. Consolidate with existing context/default/configuration and fill-limit cases before freeze.

categories.name: Token-derived authentication loses account or parent validity constraints
categories.include: Creating credentials from an existing token omits required current account-status revalidation or inheritance of the parent's expiration, allowing derived authorization beyond the account/parent validity policy; inspect source token, current identity, token backend defaults and issue lifecycle.
categories.exclude: Permitted refresh policies, ordinary password-only errors, session revocation without credential chaining, or assuming distinct validity submechanisms in one CVE are automatically one independent issue.
categories.notes: Keystone token branch trusts embedded user status after disable; one patch rechecks current identity. Successive patch carries old expires to avoid renewed default lifetime. Same CVE/mechanical family and shared function snapshot, but account-disable, password revocation and expiration submechanisms require explicit independence/negative-scope decisions.

categories.name: Arithmetic dispatch omits required zero-operand result normalization
categories.include: An admitted arithmetic path omits established zero-operand handling, returning a wrong infinity/NaN/value classification; inspect operation direction, dtype, missing-value fill and matched scalar/vector contract.
categories.exclude: All-zero normalization requiring finite/zero output covered separately, warning suppression without numerical change, or claiming every zero denominator should yield infinity.
categories.notes: Pandas raw-array reverse floor division with fill_value omits dispatch_fill_zeros, producing wrong NaN versus Inf. Retained regression establishes numerical contract separately from warning-only changes; exact helper/version semantics remain contextual.

categories.name: Bearer token is exposed in a backend object/request URI retained in logs
categories.include: A live bearer credential is embedded in a backend object/request path logged outside the token's intended audience, permitting replay by log readers; inspect token lifecycle, URI producer, request/log sink and access conditions.
categories.exclude: Every URI containing an identifier, command argument or validator-message disclosure, or assuming token-derived opaque object naming secures all inbound URLs, headers, caches and historical logs.
categories.notes: Swauth raw token becomes Swift .token object name and backend GET/PUT/DELETE URI. Coordinated SHA512-derived naming removes raw bearer from that storage path; memcache keys and remote validation URLs still use raw token. Requires matching object producers, migration and affected logging policy.

categories.name: Fixed-width text storage truncates a required replacement value
categories.include: Text conversion allocates fixed-width storage sized before a required replacement is inserted, silently truncating that value under an existing serialization contract; inspect width selection, assignment and output consumer.
categories.exclude: Lossy text encoding, source whitespace formatting, general memory corruption, or claiming replacement-width allocation preserves all longer original values.
categories.notes: Pandas CSV native conversion infers Unicode width from existing values, then inserts na_rep. Regression establishes a longer null marker is truncated; explicit na_rep width repairs that case but mixed longer non-null values require separate scrutiny. Correctness scope still pending.

categories.name: Authentication lookup conflates distinct external identities under database collation
categories.include: An authentication identity lookup relies on database equality whose collation admits distinct case-sensitive external identifiers, returning another principal's account; inspect external ID contract, effective collation and exact-result verification.
categories.exclude: Intentional case-insensitive usernames, equivalent policy-value normalization, ordinary metadata casing, or assuming all databases/collations conflate these identifiers.
categories.notes: social-app-django MySQL/MariaDB uid lookup may return a case-insensitive match for a different third-party uid. Fix filters candidates then requires exact Python uid equality; provider identity and historical schema uniqueness remain contextual.

categories.name: Reconstruction drops required semantic metadata
categories.include: Object reconstruction omits existing semantic metadata required for downstream lookup or structural roundtrip, such as index names becoming column identities; inspect the metadata producer and functional consumer.
categories.exclude: Display preferences without a functional contract, new metadata features, dtype conversion covered by dtype preservation, or position/value misalignment without metadata loss.
categories.notes: Categorical group index omits self.name, losing original group column identity on reset_index. Not just output typography. Existing metadata-normalization/context categories still require consolidation from training evidence.

categories.name: Lower-trust value is spliced into template source before evaluation
categories.include: Request/data text is concatenated into trusted template source and subsequently evaluated as template syntax instead of bound as a value; inspect composition, render call and input reachability.
categories.exclude: Intentionally user-authored template source lacking a sandbox, HTML-only escaping, or claiming arbitrary host execution without engine/capability evidence.
categories.notes: psiTurk inserts request mode into HTML source before render_template_string. Coordinated helper inserts fixed {{ mode }} placeholder and caller passes mode as data. Source/data separation, not a claim that arbitrary templates are sandboxed.

categories.name: Allocated buffer does not cover the copy primitive's write extent
categories.include: Buffer allocation covers logical content length but not a word-rounded or otherwise larger write span required by its copy primitive, permitting corruption across the intended memory boundary; inspect allocator, offsets, copy contract and reachable layout.
categories.exclude: Python memory unsafety inferred solely from byte-array operations, unbounded input resource consumption, or claiming every invocation corrupts live data without layout and length preconditions.
categories.notes: Vyper concat IR uses byte offsets into a logical-length allocation while copy_bytes may store a full 32-byte word. Extra allocation provides padding while logical output type remains unchanged. EVM contract memory corruption, not Python host buffer overflow; supplemental core.py must be retained/pinned.

categories.name: Security-token comparison uses a data-dependent equality operation
categories.include: A reachable secret/token verification uses ordinary equality rather than an appropriate timing-resistant primitive, exposing a conditional comparison oracle; inspect token stability, runtime semantics, request path and observability.
categories.exclude: Every equality operation, public values, claims of practical remote recovery without timing evidence, or assuming a comparison change repairs token lifecycle, replay or every cryptographic weakness.
categories.notes: Oppia CSRF validator compares reconstructed token with ==; coordinated change uses compare_digest on bytes plus nonce/SHA256 token format. Advisory's one-second limit needs reconciliation: old verifier recomputes using submitted issued_on, not necessarily current second. No timing attack reproduced.

categories.name: A consumer requiring sorted data receives admitted unsorted input
categories.include: A supported unsorted input is passed to an algorithm whose established contract requires monotonic/sorted reference data, producing incorrect results; inspect consumer semantics and coordinated permutation of associated values.
categories.exclude: Forbidden unsorted input, arbitrary sorting preferences, label/position identity errors without a sorting precondition, or claiming sorting resolves duplicate-coordinate or every numerical edge case.
categories.notes: NumPy interpolation requires increasing reference x; Pandas accepts descending/unsorted indexes. Fix sorts valid reference x and matching y together while preserving query/output order.

categories.name: Credential verification permits repeated guesses without required throttling
categories.include: A reachable credential-check path exposes repeated guesses without the intended attempt bound, lockout or equivalent effective rate control; inspect session/authentication prerequisites, verification and policy enforcement.
categories.exclude: Every login without a local counter, existing effective external throttles, missing reauthentication where no verification existed, or claiming a per-session logout is global/account-level rate limiting.
categories.notes: rdiffweb current-password change check gains five-failure session logout; old nonempty current password was already checked by set_password. Authenticated-session guessing and external controls remain contextual.

categories.name: Redirect method conversion retains a sensitive request body
categories.include: Automatic redirect changes a body-bearing request to GET but retains sensitive body content for a destination outside its intended audience; inspect recursion, status/method conversion and destination trust.
categories.exclude: Credential headers stripped under a separate policy, unchanged-method redirects, redirects without sensitive content, or assuming every 301/302/303 branch is affected identically.
categories.notes: urllib3 PoolManager 303 branch changes method only; fix clears body and prepares entity headers before recursive request. Compromised redirecting/destination service and sensitive content are prerequisites.

categories.name: Lower-trust malformed text aborts processing at an unhandled decoding boundary
categories.include: Admitted lower-trust bytes raise an unhandled decoding error across an established availability boundary; inspect effective encoding, error policy, catch scope and entry point.
categories.exclude: Any Unicode failure assumed security relevant, forbidden malformed inputs, or claiming request/CLI abortion demonstrates process-wide or distributed denial of service.
categories.notes: markdown-it-py CLI file reader catches OSError but not UnicodeDecodeError. UTF-8 errors=ignore avoids that decode failure; dropped bytes and stdout encoding remain separate issues.

categories.name: Transformation loses a required semantic dtype
categories.include: A supported transformation converts values through a generic representation and loses a dtype required by its existing contract, changing subsequent operations or roundtrip identity; inspect conversion and reconstruction.
categories.exclude: New dtype support without an existing requirement, documented intentional coercion, shape-only errors or preservation claims without extension-type semantics.
categories.notes: Homogeneous extension-typed DataFrame transpose passes through generic .values and loses extension dtype. New per-row extension reconstruction preserves it, but dictionary construction can collapse duplicate source index labels.

categories.name: Label-based alignment loses required positional identity
categories.include: Deduplication or label-based reindexing replaces distinct required positions or assigns values to the wrong labels, violating an established index/value correspondence; inspect duplicate-label semantics, operation mode and expected mapping.
categories.exclude: Intentional label aggregation, counting repeated representations of one entity, unsupported duplicate labels, or shape differences without an index/value identity defect.
categories.notes: pct_change without frequency already preserves positions; unconditional index deduplication and reindex broadcast first occurrence results over distinct repeated labels. Frequency-based alignment retains its separate policy.

categories.name: Lower-trust field size is unbounded before resource-consuming processing
categories.include: A reachable lower-trust field exceeds its intended size limit and is accepted for storage or resource-consuming processing across an availability boundary; inspect validation, caller, consumer and effective upstream limits.
categories.exclude: Every missing length check, harmless large trusted inputs, regex backtracking without a size/storage mechanism, or claiming a per-field cap bounds whole requests, request frequency or all resource use.
categories.notes: Sydent client-secret regex allows arbitrarily long matching strings; request-token caller forwards them after validation. New 255-character cap limits accepted field size; downstream persistence and server body limits still need pinning.

categories.name: A consumer ignores an established configuration override
categories.include: An operation uses a hardcoded fallback despite an established environment/configuration override selecting its resource location or behaviour; inspect the existing configuration producer, consumer and explicit-argument precedence.
categories.exclude: New configuration features without an old supported contract, intended per-operation overrides, security trust of configuration sources, or unsupported claims that all consumers dynamically reload settings.
categories.notes: Keras backend already honours KERAS_HOME but get_file defaults to ~/.keras. Explicit cache_dir retains priority and unwritable-directory fallback remains. Supplemental backend source must be retained/pinned before approval.

categories.name: An admitted empty contribution produces a zero normalization denominator
categories.include: An accepted all-zero mask or other empty contribution set reaches normalization by zero, violating an established finite/zero-result contract; inspect denominator construction, producer admissibility and numerical runtime semantics.
categories.exclude: Unsupported zero inputs, arbitrary epsilon changes, resource-availability claims without a security boundary, or assuming one stabilized denominator repairs unrelated zero divisions or nonfinite inputs.
categories.notes: All-zero Keras mask yields masked score zero and mean(mask)=0; adding positive backend epsilon avoids this 0/0. All-zero sample weights retain a separate unchanged denominator.

categories.name: Lower-trust metadata supplies privileged internal request options
categories.include: Lower-trust URL or content metadata is merged into headers/options interpreted internally as privileged network controls, such as proxy selection, without the intended allowlist; inspect metadata preservation, request consumer and control-header handling.
categories.exclude: Ordinary outgoing HTTP header content without an internal control boundary, arbitrary SSRF inferred from a constrained extractor URL, or unconditional cookie disclosure despite TLS/secure-cookie policy.
categories.notes: yt-dlp Vimeo unsmuggles arbitrary http_headers into requests; clean_proxies consumes Ytdl-Request-Proxy as routing control. Fix permits only referer metadata. Generic advisory reachability and Vimeo URL constraints remain distinct.

categories.name: Sensitive credential change accepts a session without required reauthentication
categories.include: An authenticated session can change a sensitive credential without the required current-password or equivalent step-up verification; inspect session prerequisites, credential mutation and actual reauthentication policy.
categories.exclude: Unauthenticated login fail-open, authorized recovery/reset flows, arbitrary missing password prompts, or assuming all authenticated actions require reauthentication.
categories.notes: ZenML self-password update previously requires only active session; fix requires and verifies old password. Other-user password-update prohibition is a separate authorization policy, not proof of a preexisting global permission bypass.

categories.name: Credentialed CORS origin policy omits a hostname boundary
categories.include: An attacker-controlled origin passes a hostname suffix check without the required label/authority boundary, receiving credentialed CORS approval; inspect reflected allow-origin, credential flag, configured host and browser cookie policy together.
categories.exclude: Every reflected origin, wildcard responses without usable credentials, CSRF inferred without a state-changing consumer, or universal cross-site cookie access independent of browser policy.
categories.notes: Sentry endswith(basehost) permits an unrelated hostname ending in the same characters. New delimiter-aware suffixes restrict this check; base-hostname is empty by default and cookie blocking limits practical impact. Nested wrapper and outer decorator overlap.

categories.name: Inclusive endpoint is omitted by an exclusive range or count
categories.include: A documented inclusive index endpoint is treated as exclusive when enumerating, sampling or counting supported elements, omitting a valid boundary element or batch; inspect endpoint initialization and caller iteration counts together.
categories.exclude: An intentionally half-open range, newly introduced endpoint semantics, or assuming a local range repair also fixes an unchanged upstream batch count.
categories.notes: Keras TimeseriesGenerator defaults end_index to len(data)-1 but passes it as exclusive high/stop. Coordinated __len__ repair is also needed when the omitted endpoint requires another batch.

categories.name: Key derivation block accounting violates requested key length
categories.include: Cryptographic derivation uses incorrect digest units or generated-block accounting, returning too little key material or violating valid output limits; inspect algorithm byte units, empty accumulators and consumer length handling.
categories.exclude: Generic hashing, unsupported claims that every short output is accepted as a key, or declaring all KDF security repaired by a length fix.
categories.notes: HKDF expansion counts an empty initial block and divides a byte digest_size by eight. Small positive requests can return empty; actual boundary is the inspected loop, not advisory shorthand.

categories.name: Lower-trust XML entity expansion exceeds the intended parsing policy
categories.include: A reachable lower-trust XML input can declare/expand entities under a parser policy permitting excessive work; inspect preprocessing, parser/runtime limits and entity rejection rather than inferring vulnerability from XML use.
categories.exclude: Automatic external-file/entity-read claims for ElementTree, entity declarations removed by preprocessing without a demonstrated bypass, or universal resource-safety claims from entity rejection.
categories.notes: LangChain completion parser replaces standard ElementTree with defusedxml. Internal entity expansion depends on Expat protections; synchronous streaming strips pre-root text and needs distinct reachability evidence.

categories.name: Validation diagnostics disclose sensitive input to a lower-trust log
categories.include: Validation messages containing sensitive values or input fragments are emitted to a log accessible outside the input's intended audience; inspect validator formatting, input provenance, caller mode and log access.
categories.exclude: Every diagnostic log, secret argument exposure in another category, or assuming a new optional suppression flag makes default calls confidential.
categories.notes: cloud-init schema messages can contain hashed passwords; coordinated boot caller disables detail logging. Default log_details=True and strict exceptions still disclose details by design.

categories.name: Security-policy producer and consumer disagree on case normalization
categories.include: Security policy admits equivalent mixed-case values but persists/forwards them without canonicalization to a case-sensitive enforcement consumer, omitting required restrictions; inspect accepted input, stored representation and enforcement branch.
categories.exclude: Cosmetic casing, generic metadata conversion, redaction/header normalization already categorized separately, or assuming a case-sensitive check fails open without tracing resulting enforcement.
categories.notes: Nova accepts protocol names through upper-case validation but stores original spelling; firewall lowercase-only branches omit port/type limits. Producer now lowercases; consumer fix also canonicalizes existing stored rules.

categories.name: Text-stream newline translation duplicates CSV record boundaries
categories.include: CSV writer record terminators interact with runtime text-stream newline translation to introduce extra machine-observable rows; inspect writer dialect, stream settings, runtime and established record-count contract.
categories.exclude: Line-ending preferences without a record/consumer contract, source newline roundtrip, or assuming every Python/platform branch has duplicate translation.
categories.notes: Keras CSVLogger Python-3 Windows text stream translates the newline in csv.excel CRLF again. New io.open receives newline='\n' from coordinated constructor; regression checks physical row and column counts.

categories.name: Tensor transformation discards or mismatches required axes
categories.include: An established tensor/array contract requires axes or rank to be preserved/aligned, but reshaping, flattening or shape construction removes or mismatches them, producing wrong broadcasting, comparison or rejected valid inputs.
categories.exclude: Unsupported shapes introduced as a feature, arbitrary numerical differences, or claims about every backend without inspecting operation semantics.
categories.notes: Flattening sparse labels collapses sample/time axes while argmax predictions retain them. Rank-aware singleton squeeze preserves the comparison shape.

categories.name: Untrusted parsed content reaches an invalid non-null token assumption
categories.include: A reachable lower-trust parse/render path admits absent token children or attributes but asserts or consumes them as present, aborting processing across an availability boundary; inspect producer invariants and the actual failing consumer.
categories.exclude: Assertions on unreachable states, arbitrary externally constructed objects without a lower-trust path, or treating one request failure as demonstrated process-wide denial of service.
categories.notes: markdown-it-py nested image parser can assign children=None; renderInlineAsText asserts that a nested image has children even though its entry iteration already accepts None. Other same-fix guards require independent reachability evidence.

categories.name: Untrusted record delimiters forge entries in a text log
categories.include: Lower-trust values containing record delimiters are embedded unescaped into a line-oriented log, allowing forged or corrupted records; inspect input provenance and sink/formatter behaviour.
categories.exclude: Secret disclosure through otherwise well-formed logs, every interpolated log value, or assuming CR/LF escaping secures all terminals, encodings or structured logging consumers.
categories.notes: pyLoad API login logs request usernames even on failed authentication. Fix replaces CR/LF with literal backslash sequences; advisory demonstrates the sibling UI login, not automatically the API route. No request or payload executed.

categories.name: Sensitive log output has excessive filesystem read permissions
categories.include: Sensitive process output reaches a file readable by principals outside its intended audience because file-creation or retained permissions, or log-sink process identity, are insufficient; inspect sensitive writers, sink configuration and effective file-mode enforcement.
categories.exclude: Every log labelled sensitive, shell injection inferred from an authorized sink command, or a umask change claimed to revoke permissions on existing files or repair all output modes.
categories.notes: cloud-init restricts log-sink subprocess umask/GID in one fix; a separate later fix enforces restrictive mode on existing logs. A umask change alone never repairs existing modes. Sensitive writers, direct redirection and effective filesystem policy still need review.

categories.name: Build or cache workspace accepts an existing lower-trust directory
categories.include: A predictable build/cache directory is reused based only on existence or writability without required ownership, permission or symlink checks, allowing another local user to supply artifacts; inspect directory selection and artifact consumers.
categories.exclude: Secure atomic creation alone treated as vulnerable, arbitrary filesystem traversal, race-free guarantees from separate path checks, or POSIX ownership guarantees applied to Windows ACLs without evidence.
categories.notes: SciPy weave default directory accepts pre-existing writable locations for compiled modules/catalogs. Coordinated helpers validate POSIX owner/mode and reject symlinks; pathname checks do not establish race-free or universal Windows security.

categories.name: Untrusted literal identity or path is interpreted as authorization regex syntax
categories.include: Lower-trust identity/path data is interpolated into a security-policy regular expression without literal escaping, broadening authorized matches; inspect policy templates, data admission and the permission consumer.
categories.exclude: Backtracking complexity, administrator-authored regex rules, ordinary matching of untrusted text against a fixed pattern, or a claim that escaping these interpolation defaults secures every dynamic substitution.
categories.notes: Radicale owner templates interpolate login into an anchored collection regex; authenticated metacharacter usernames can broaden ownership. Fix escapes login/path defaults; later captured-group format substitution remains a separate boundary. No regex or exploit executed.

categories.name: Privileged mutation is reachable through a request method intended to be read-only
categories.include: A privileged state-changing branch accepts GET or another intended safe request method because the required submission-method guard is absent; inspect request parameter binding, the mutation helper and effective method checks.
categories.exclude: Read-only handlers, a method restriction already enforced elsewhere, or treating POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE acceptance alone as complete token/origin-based CSRF protection.
categories.notes: rdiffweb user deletion previously validated fields without checking submission method. validate_on_submit adds a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE gate and blocks the evidenced GET deletion; it does not introduce an unpredictable token or origin check.

categories.name: Failure is classified with the wrong machine-observable error status
categories.include: An established invalid-input/operation outcome is reported through the wrong exception or exit-status class, affecting a documented or regression-established machine-consumer contract; inspect actual framework handling, not wording alone.
categories.exclude: Diagnostic wording-only edits, changing one nonzero code without an established contract, or assuming failed input was previously accepted successfully when it already raised a different error.
categories.notes: Missing explicit --config reaches FileError (exit 1) before; Click path existence validation classifies it as an invalid parameter (exit 2) after. Existing callback already rejects the missing file.

categories.name: Privileged state-changing request lacks required anti-forgery binding
categories.include: A lower-trust page can cause a privileged ambient-context state change without the required unpredictable token or origin/initiator binding; inspect the state-changing consumer and real request-scheme/backend reachability.
categories.exclude: Read-only resources, missing tokens where another effective request-binding mechanism is established, credential-source disagreement classified separately, or automatic code-execution claims without the downstream trigger.
categories.notes: qutebrowser local qute://settings/set changes browser configuration from a request URL. Fix adds token checking plus coordinated backend initiator checks; changing editor.command alone is not proof a command already ran.

categories.name: Untrusted outbound destinations bypass the required network-address policy
categories.include: A server-side request path accepts a lower-trust destination but uses a client or resolver that omits required IP-range restrictions; inspect destination provenance, request consumer, client construction and effective configuration.
categories.exclude: Browser open redirects, a mere client getter rename, ordinary trusted-service requests, or a claim that client substitution blocks all SSRF regardless of configured ranges, DNS, redirects or proxy routing.
categories.notes: Synapse key-revocation and push consumers gain an IP-policy client. This exact fix still requires effective ip_range_blacklist configuration; deprecated federation-only ranges do not automatically cover these paths.

categories.name: Security indicator forgets an exception across the protected object's lifecycle
categories.include: A displayed security decision uses transient state that is reset while an underlying security exception remains effective, falsely reporting the protected resource as verified; inspect exception writers, reset events, status consumer and actual warning policy.
categories.exclude: Cosmetic colour preferences, a certificate verification bypass inferred solely from an indicator, or an ordinary stale UI value without a security assurance contract.
categories.notes: qutebrowser resets a per-load SSL-error flag although accepted certificate exceptions can persist; new shared host history preserves warning status. This repairs an assurance indicator, not the user's certificate-acceptance policy.

categories.name: Non-cryptographic randomness used for a security-sensitive unpredictable value
categories.include: A security-sensitive nonce/authenticator/secret requires unpredictability but is generated using a non-cryptographic PRNG; inspect generator binding and actual protocol consumer.
categories.exclude: Ordinary simulation/random selection, short identifiers without an unpredictability requirement, or a claim that secure randomness repairs every weakness in the surrounding protocol.
categories.notes: pyrad's sixteen-byte RADIUS authenticator uses module random.randrange before the fix and a module-bound random.SystemRandom afterwards; consumer participates in password hiding and reply verification. No recovery attack or entropy measurement executed.

categories.name: Untrusted data is reconstructed as executable Python expression text
categories.include: Lower-trust values are interpolated into Python source passed to eval or an equivalent evaluator, allowing data to alter executable syntax; inspect actual data provenance and evaluation scope.
categories.exclude: AST parsing without evaluation, fixed trusted expressions, shell-command injection, or assuming an allowlist of outer function names neutralizes interpolated arguments.
categories.notes: Eve reconstructs ObjectId call text from an AST string value before eval; direct constructor calls remove this second source interpretation.

categories.name: Automatic configuration search includes a lower-trust execution source
categories.include: Automatic configuration discovery searches a lower-trust location and loads executable configuration under the invoking user's privileges without explicit selection; inspect path precedence and loading consumer.
categories.exclude: Explicitly authorized configuration files, ordinary data-only lookup without an execution boundary, or a claim that removing automatic CWD insertion secures every configurable path.
categories.notes: Jupyter prepends current working directory to config search; fix removes implicit CWD entry while explicit config_dir and environment-derived paths remain.

categories.name: Expected recoverable input condition aborts the surrounding operation
categories.include: A supported input or execution-environment condition raises a specific exception which should be handled locally to skip/recover and continue; source, caller and contract evidence establish recoverability.
categories.exclude: Blanket exception suppression, unexpected failures that should propagate, or assuming all filesystem exceptions have the same recovery policy.
categories.notes: Outside-root symlink resolution makes relative_to raise ValueError and abort file discovery; fix skips only symlinks and rethrows other ValueErrors.

categories.name: Indexing assumes a supported sequence is nonempty
categories.include: Direct indexing raises on an empty sequence admitted by the input contract; fix uses an empty-safe access or guard and preserves the required empty-input behaviour.
categories.exclude: Inputs forbidden to be empty, missing None dereference guards, or attributing unrelated empty-input failures to the changed access.
categories.notes: src_txt[-1] raises for empty source; [-1:] is empty-safe. File byte decoding has a separate same-fix empty-input repair.

categories.name: Textual URL prefix accepts a different authority across a request boundary
categories.include: A security restriction uses raw URL prefix matching rather than a parsed authority comparison, allowing an untrusted different-host URL to reach a downstream request path; inspect URL normalization and consumer.
categories.exclude: Ordinary URL joining, open redirects without server-side fetching, or claiming a netloc check eliminates DNS, redirects, same-host or all SSRF risks.
categories.notes: LangChain recursive links can use a hostname extending the base URL string; new exact netloc check supplements rather than replaces path-prefix policy.

categories.name: Input newline convention is lost at a text output boundary
categories.include: Input decoding normalizes newline information which output must preserve under an established byte/format contract; inspect both read and write settings and decide non-style eligibility.
categories.exclude: Every newline normalization labelled a defect, runtime bytes/text encoding mismatch without newline involvement, or unsupported claims of preserving every mixed line ending.
categories.notes: Black detects one source newline convention and reuses it for output; non-style task eligibility remains unresolved and mixed-newline/empty inputs require separate review.

categories.name: Authorization subject can change between identification and policy evaluation
categories.include: Authorization identifies a requester through a mutable/reusable identifier and evaluates privileges after the represented subject can change; inspect identity lookup, policy API and affected runtime.
categories.exclude: Generic races without an authorization boundary, stable subject identifiers without substitution evidence, or a claim that any bus-name check repairs all policy bypasses.
categories.notes: Polkit unix-process PID/start-time zero subject replaced with authenticated system-bus-name; local D-Bus and policy conditions remain contextual.

categories.name: Redirect handling fails to remove credentials across an origin boundary
categories.include: Sensitive request headers survive a redirect to a different origin because the removal policy or header-name comparison is incomplete; inspect header representation, retry policy and origin predicate.
categories.exclude: Open redirect without credential forwarding, secret redaction at an output sink, or assuming a particular header mapping is case-sensitive without evidence.
categories.notes: urllib3 removal is case-sensitive on ordinary mappings; coordinated Retry normalization and incomplete-fix lineage CVE-2018-20060 matter.

categories.name: Authentication lifecycle change preserves sessions that require invalidation
categories.include: A logout, invalid-authentication or credential-change path omits required session invalidation/rotation or revocation of other authenticated sessions; inspect the session backend, persistence boundary and surrounding authentication lifecycle.
categories.exclude: Every session.clear call labelled fixation, unrelated stale UI state, or inferring complete logout/login safety from one corrected branch.
categories.notes: Horizon invalid-session branch delegates to logout/flush; rdiffweb password change deletes other database sessions while retaining the current session. Different lifecycle submechanisms share this provisional category but not an issue family; backend semantics and persistence remain contextual.

categories.name: Lower-trust template source evaluated without the required sandbox
categories.include: Attacker-controlled template source reaches a template engine with capabilities beyond its intended trust boundary; distinguish executable template source from values passed into a fixed template.
categories.exclude: Ordinary trusted templates, assuming context strings are recursively interpreted as template source, or treating sandboxing as HTML escaping or a universal resource bound.
categories.notes: MLflow CardTab renders self.template in ordinary Jinja; lower-trust template provenance and privilege boundary remain unresolved, so seed is ambiguous.

categories.name: Regular expression permits excessive backtracking on untrusted input
categories.include: Overlapping/ambiguous repeated regex components cause excessive matching work on a supported untrusted input family; inspect the actual pattern, engine and reachable call path.
categories.exclude: Regex use alone, unsupported exact complexity claims, or ordinary linear scanning labelled ReDoS without pattern/failure-path evidence.
categories.notes: Overlapping whitespace/tab repeats followed by a required non-whitespace character; function-only input omits the module-level pattern. No adversarial execution performed.

categories.name: Missing restriction on embedding a sensitive UI in frames
categories.include: A web application omits an intended anti-framing response policy, permitting UI redressing under the affected browser/deployment conditions; inspect response-hook registration and advisory context.
categories.exclude: Generic XSS or CSRF inferred from missing headers, or assuming clickjacking remains possible where an equivalent effective frame-ancestors/proxy policy exists.
categories.notes: Application factory registers a new after_request X-Frame-Options DENY hook; effective other middleware/proxy policy and sensitive UI actions remain contextual.

categories.name: Attacker-controlled input multiplicity amplifies expensive work
categories.include: Untrusted input count or repetition drives expensive operations without an adequate bound/deduplication/batching policy, with evidence of an availability boundary and affected call path.
categories.exclude: Any linear loop labelled denial of service, ordinary performance improvements without attacker reachability, or a batching fix claimed to bound all CPU/memory work.
categories.notes: Nova affinity hints trigger one compute lookup per supplied UUID, including duplicates; new map avoids that lookup multiplicity but still scales with instance/input counts.

categories.name: Unsafe inline rendering policy for untrusted uploaded content
categories.include: A serving/proxy path overrides upload safety metadata and permits inline rendering of attacker-controlled active content; establish Content-Type, disposition, origin and proxy behaviour.
categories.exclude: Generic missing HTML escaping, harmless filename changes, or unconditional XSS claims where CSP/browser/storage configuration already mitigates execution.
categories.notes: S3 Content-Type versus app disposition mismatch; preserve S3 policy and use signed attachment override. Requires proxy/cache and browser context.

categories.name: Sensitive-field matching misses equivalent key representations
categories.include: A sensitive-field policy uses inconsistent key/path normalization and omits protected values from redaction; establish actual key representation, policy and lower-trust output sink.
categories.exclude: Assuming added sensitive-field policy entries prove an existing case-normalization defect, or treating all missing redaction as a selected-function log leak.
categories.notes: Tentative case-sensitive matching mechanism; real mixed-case sensitive inputs remain unestablished. Same patch also expands the policy outside the selected function.

categories.name: Sensitive values exposed through command arguments and diagnostic propagation
categories.include: Secret contents are embedded in process arguments that can be retained in exceptions, logs or command auditing; inspect the runner and disclosure conditions.
categories.exclude: Shell injection inferred from an argument list, assuming all process arguments are publicly readable, or claiming file transport makes all metadata/diagnostics confidential.
categories.notes: Juju secret commands preserve CalledProcessError as exception cause; access to resulting logs is an additional prerequisite.

categories.name: Position calculations mix incompatible counting units
categories.include: A position/length is compared with another measured in different units, such as raw character offsets versus expanded display columns; consumer/caller establishes the unit contract.
categories.exclude: Arbitrary numeric changes or formatter presentation cases admitted without checking task eligibility.
categories.notes: Mechanism supported by len(indent) caller; comment-indentation-only task eligibility remains unresolved.

categories.name: Omitted option is replaced with a value that overrides required downstream defaults
categories.include: A caller or serializer turns an omitted optional setting into an explicit value, preventing the documented downstream default/automatic selection; inspect both ends of the option flow.
categories.exclude: Intentional documented defaults or an assumed server policy without supporting evidence.
categories.notes: Two functions jointly preserve omitted pool quantity and omit --quantity; one shared issue family.

categories.name: Path normalization discards meaningful root or separator structure
categories.include: Path splitting/joining loses structural markers required by a supported path grammar; source/fix evidence establishes the intended root and resulting path.
categories.exclude: Security confinement claims, URL composition or unsupported path formats inferred only from platform names.
categories.notes: Dropping empty backslash-separated components destroys a UNC root. No general safety claim for all joins.

categories.name: TLS connection omits required server identity verification
categories.include: A TLS client uses a non-verifying context/default where certificate and hostname authentication are required; library/runtime and configuration evidence must support that behaviour.
categories.exclude: Claiming encryption implies authentication, treating every missing explicit context as vulnerable regardless of library defaults, or assuming plaintext modes are repaired.
categories.notes: SMTP_SSL/STARTTLS defaults in the affected runtime; explicit SERVER_AUTH context repairs configured TLS paths, not mandatory transport encryption.

categories.name: Filesystem operation escapes its permitted root
categories.include: An untrusted path reaches a filesystem operation without ensuring that its resolved target remains inside the intended root; caller/helper evidence establishes the boundary.
categories.exclude: Authorized arbitrary-path selection, mere relative-path use without a trust boundary, and claims that a pre-operation realpath check eliminates filesystem races.
categories.notes: Guest image file injection joins untrusted path to mount root and writes as root; after helper checks realpath plus directory separator. No race-free or universal symlink-safety claim.

categories.name: Untrusted values interpolated into SQL syntax
categories.include: Values potentially originating from untrusted input, including stored values, are concatenated into SQL without safe parameter binding; inspect provenance and the execution sink.
categories.exclude: Generated placeholder names concatenated while values remain bound, or assuming every database read contains attacker-controlled content.
categories.notes: Stored user IDs interpolated into an IN clause; user creation/identifier constraints and database adapter remain conditional context.

categories.name: Incorrect caller context passed to a decision-making helper
categories.include: A helper receives a substituted or incomplete identity/context instead of the actual caller context, changing an established branch or required operation; both caller and consumer must be inspected.
categories.exclude: Diagnostic-only identity differences without an established correctness contract, and security-boundary identity mismatches assigned to a security category.
categories.notes: An installed collection is passed as its own parent instead of preserving parent=None for a top-level requirement. Black-6 also loses target-dependent tokenizer mode when forwarding grammar alone. Each coordinated repair keeps its own shared family, not multiple independent issues.

categories.name: Metadata representation is not normalized for its consumer
categories.include: Parsed metadata of an accepted but unexpected type/empty representation is passed to a consumer requiring a normalized form; source traces establish the incompatible operation and intended fallback/coercion.
categories.exclude: General text-encoding defects, speculative schema validation gaps, or a claim that a narrow conversion validates all metadata.
categories.notes: Numeric manifest versions reach string split through constructor/add_requirement; empty version fallback is limited to the documented resolver case.

categories.name: CSRF validation bypass through inconsistent credential-source selection
categories.include: A caller decides whether CSRF validation is required using different missing/empty credential semantics from a helper that falls back to ambient cookies, enabling a cookie-authenticated operation without its required CSRF check.
categories.exclude: Token error-code changes without evidence they bypass CSRF, or treating every falsey/defaulting expression as a CSRF defect.
categories.notes: Requires cross-function source/guard reasoning; the cookie fallback function alone does not show the missing CSRF check.

categories.name: A supported input or platform case is omitted
categories.include: A branch restricts processing to an incomplete set of documented/supported cases, causing a valid alternative to be misclassified or skipped; source/fix evidence establishes that alternative.
categories.exclude: Unsupported-platform feature additions or an assumed missing case without a demonstrated existing behaviour requirement.
categories.notes: Kali identification from os-release as well as legacy lsb-release; this label does not establish correctness of every release-field parser.

categories.name: Insufficient shell-specific escaping of untrusted command data
categories.include: Untrusted data enters shell command text without sufficient shell-specific quoting/escaping, either absent or using rules that fail to neutralize that shell's expansion/special-character semantics; platform, helper and command-use evidence must support the mechanism.
categories.exclude: Generic subprocess use, POSIX-only assumptions applied to Windows, or a claim that any general quoting helper guarantees all command contexts safe.
categories.notes: Windows cmd percent expansion in q-format/--exec path; related incomplete fix CVE-2023-40581 needs root-cause-family review rather than automatic independent counting.

categories.name: Duplicate representations counted as distinct entities
categories.include: Multiple fields/representations of one entity increment an aggregate that should count the entity once; supported data shape and fix establish the unit.
categories.exclude: Arbitrary arithmetic errors, intentional per-field counts, or incorrect architecture assumptions without source evidence.
categories.notes: POWER cpuinfo processor and cpu entries describe the same logical CPU; architecture absence remains a separate limitation.

categories.name: Overbroad global/class resolution or object construction during deserialization
categories.include: Deserialization permits lower-trust input to resolve globals/classes or construct objects beyond the intended safe type/module/name allowlist; inspect resolver or loader policy, input provenance and version-dependent constructors.
categories.exclude: General authentication labels copied from metadata, arbitrary import usage outside deserialization, or claims that every class in a repaired allowlist is safe.
categories.notes: Shinken removes a namespace-prefix bypass; pystemon switches main/included YAML to safe constructors but its lower-trust config boundary remains ambiguous. Neither repair proves universal deserialization safety; do not equate all FullLoader versions with unsafe legacy Loader.

categories.name: Incorrect conditional or ordering of state-changing operations
categories.include: An operation required for a valid state transition is omitted or ordered incorrectly; expected transition semantics must be established beyond a changed conditional alone.
categories.exclude: Assuming a skipped branch omits an operation when another branch already emits it, or inferring device-state semantics solely from a small patch.
categories.notes: Tentative seed: VRF branch already emits state commands; changed pre/post-VRF ordering needs device/protocol context.

categories.name: Authentication failure path grants credentials or success
categories.include: Failure or nonmatching branches of a required authentication-factor check reach a credential/success sink instead of rejection, supported by source/fix evidence.
categories.exclude: Resource authorization defects after valid authentication, merely absent rate limiting, or token issuance already gated by an external check not yet inspected.
categories.notes: Do not equate MFA bypass after password validation with passwordless or arbitrary-account compromise.

categories.name: Incorrect base/path composition for API navigation
categories.include: An API prefix is duplicated or a required path component lost when composing a continuation/resource URL; exact helper semantics and expected response shape support the failure.
