categories.exclude: Automatic assumptions about urllib.urljoin, generic networking failures or SSRF without a demonstrated security boundary.
categories.notes: Source _urljoin is a string path join, not standard urllib URL resolution.

categories.name: Missing resource-scoped authorization or credential binding
categories.include: A token, session or authenticated principal is accepted for a resource without the required resource/tenant binding or access check, with source/advisory support.
categories.exclude: Identity-format mismatches without an authorization boundary, merely absent authentication decorators, or access checks performed elsewhere but not yet inspected.
categories.notes: Invitation validity is distinct from authorization to use it for the current request's organization.

categories.name: Ambiguous delimiter handling across input formats
categories.include: A separator used in one accepted input format is incorrectly applied to another, corrupting a valid value; fix distinguishes formats before splitting.
categories.exclude: Security URL-policy claims or malformed inputs unsupported by the documented accepted formats.
categories.notes: Colon in an HTTP(S) URL or existing file path must not be interpreted as the collection-version separator.

categories.name: Inconsistent resource identity across security-relevant operations
categories.include: Redundant request/event resource identifiers can disagree while related validation or state-building operations use different identities; source/advisory connects the mismatch to a security consequence.
categories.exclude: Ordinary identifier refactoring, generic resource-exhaustion labels or unrelated CVE-level CWE tags without function-level evidence.
categories.notes: Room identity consistency mechanism; reported federation DoS is conditional on the wider event-processing path, not a locally reproduced outcome.

categories.name: Runtime-sensitive bytes/text encoding mismatch
categories.include: Text containing supported non-ASCII characters is read, written or converted using incompatible runtime/encoding assumptions; the failure path and runtime must be established.
categories.exclude: An ordinary environment lookup assumed broken on modern Python solely because an old compatibility patch replaced it.
categories.notes: Tentative mechanism: seed commit describes UTF-8 failure, but selected function alone lacks runtime/compatibility-layer context.

categories.name: Missing None guard at a structure boundary
categories.include: Dereference of a possibly absent neighbour/sentinel at a valid boundary; fix guards the absent value.
categories.exclude: General attribute typos, arbitrary exceptions, or security impact inferred solely from module purpose.
categories.notes: Specific tail-removal mechanism only; not a claim that all boundary bugs in the function were fixed.

categories.name: Loss of meaningful whitespace in literal text
categories.include: Broad whitespace stripping changes literal user/configuration text whose boundary spaces must be preserved; source/fix intent supports that requirement.
categories.exclude: Whitespace-only style changes, intended normalisation, or unrelated parser changes in the same commit.
categories.notes: Three affected functions share one banner fix family; after-code correctness beyond space preservation is unestablished.

categories.name: Unvalidated request-controlled redirect destination
categories.include: A request-controlled URL reaches a redirect without the required host/scheme restriction, supported by source/fix evidence.
categories.exclude: Fixed internal destinations, adequately validated destinations, or authentication/authorisation defects inferred from redirect code alone.
categories.notes: Validate imported redirect/safety helper semantics; multiple functions or fixes for one CVE remain one provisional family.

categories.name: Missing context-appropriate HTML escaping
categories.include: Untrusted data reaches an HTML rendering sink without required escaping; provenance of the data and sink behaviour must be supported, not inferred from a CVE alone.
categories.exclude: JSON or URL encoding treated as HTML escaping; sanitisation changes without evidence of untrusted input or HTML rendering.
categories.notes: Tentative category from a training patch. This seed remains ambiguous: attacker control and downstream Problem rendering are not established.

categories.name: Untrusted input interpreted as a local file to read
categories.include: Input intended as data is accepted as a local file path and opened without the intended trust boundary; supporting evidence establishes untrusted reachability.
categories.exclude: Legitimate authorised file selection, arbitrary URL validation, or a disclosure/exfiltration claim without supporting evidence.
categories.notes: Function exposes a read primitive; remote provenance of the argument requires caller/advisory context.
